Certainly! Here are two hints for the problem:

**Hint 1:** Consider the structure of the design matrix. The first column $$col_0$$ is the intercept, which is always $$1$$ for all rows. The remaining columns (col_1 to col_5) represent the one-hot encoded categorical feature. Each row can only have one of these columns set to $$1$$, except for rows $$5$$ and $$6$$, which have all zeros in these columns.

**Hint 2:** One-hot encoding creates a separate column for each unique value of a categorical feature. Since rows $$0-4$$ each have exactly one of $$col_1$$ through $$col_5$$ equal to $$1$$, these columns represent unique categories. Rows $$5$$ and $$6$$, with all zeros in $$col_1$$ through $$col_5$$, indicate an additional category. Consider how many unique categories this setup implies.
